rules: Every question is about the test reports, which the knowledge graph holds beside ATT&CK v20.0.
Answers are computed by gold.py from benchmark/gold_triples.json (test split) and the ATT&CK v20.0 Enterprise file, never from the system's own graph.
A relationship that ATT&CK records for a sub-technique counts for its parent technique, because the experts' labels name parent techniques only.
'cypher' computes the same answer inside Neo4j from the ATT&CK part of the graph, with the gold facts passed as 'parameters'; gold.py --neo4j runs every query and compares the answers.

'reference_answer' states the answer in words (RAGAS context recall needs one); 'supporting_facts' lists the gold facts and the ATT&CK relationship IDs (as cited in answers: [edge:<id>]) the answer rests on.
'checked_on_attack_website', where present, names the attack.mitre.org page whose list was compared with the answer item by item, the date, and what the page lists.

questions.hops: Report -MENTIONS-> Technique <-[SUBTECHNIQUE_OF 0 or 1 step]- Technique <-MITIGATES- Mitigation, counted per mitigation
questions.question: Which MITRE ATT&CK mitigations address the largest number of the techniques described in Intel 471's December 2021 report “How the new Emotet differs from previous versions”?
questions.reference_answer: M1047 Audit addresses 5 of the 13 techniques the report describes: T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information, T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter, T1114 Email Collection, T1566 Phishing and T1606 Forge Web Credentials. No other mitigation addresses more than 4 of them.
questions.cypher:
CYPHER 25
MATCH (m:`Mitigation`)-[:`MITIGATES`]->(:`Technique`)-[:`SUBTECHNIQUE_OF`*0..1]->(t:`Technique`)
WHERE t.`attack_id` IN $techniques
WITH m, collect(DISTINCT t.`attack_id`) AS addressed
WITH max(size(addressed)) AS most, collect({id: m.`attack_id`, addressed: addressed}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row, most WHERE size(row.addressed) = most
RETURN row.id AS answer, row.addressed AS support
ORDER BY answer

questions.question: Which MITRE ATT&CK mitigations address the largest number of the techniques described in Lab52's January 2022 report “TokyoX: DLL side-loading an unknown artifact”?
questions.reference_answer: M1038 Execution Prevention and M1040 Behavior Prevention on Endpoint each address 4 of the 8 techniques the report describes. M1038 Execution Prevention addresses T1129 Shared Modules, T1204 User Execution, T1546 Event Triggered Execution (through its sub-techniques T1546.002 Screensaver, T1546.006 LC_LOAD_DYLIB Addition, T1546.008 Accessibility Features, T1546.009 AppCert DLLs and T1546.010 AppInit DLLs) and T1574 Hijack Execution Flow. M1040 Behavior Prevention on Endpoint addresses T1055 Process Injection, T1204 User Execution, T1546 Event Triggered Execution (through its sub-technique T1546.003 Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription) and T1574 Hijack Execution Flow. No other mitigation addresses more than 3 of them.
questions.cypher:
CYPHER 25
MATCH (m:`Mitigation`)-[:`MITIGATES`]->(:`Technique`)-[:`SUBTECHNIQUE_OF`*0..1]->(t:`Technique`)
WHERE t.`attack_id` IN $techniques
WITH m, collect(DISTINCT t.`attack_id`) AS addressed
WITH max(size(addressed)) AS most, collect({id: m.`attack_id`, addressed: addressed}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row, most WHERE size(row.addressed) = most
RETURN row.id AS answer, row.addressed AS support
ORDER BY answer

questions.question: Which malware or tools mentioned in Lab52's May 2021 report “Literature lover targeting Colombia with LimeRAT” does MITRE ATT&CK record as used by the threat group the report names?
questions.reference_answer: The report names the threat group G0099 APT-C-36 and the software S0385 njRAT. ATT&CK records APT-C-36 as using S0385 njRAT.

CYPHER 25
MATCH (g:`Group`)-[u:`USES`]->(s:`Software`)
WHERE g.`attack_id` IN $groups AND s.`attack_id` IN $software AND u.`source` = 'attack'
RETURN s.`attack_id` AS answer, collect(DISTINCT g.`attack_id`) AS support
ORDER BY answer

questions.question: Which of the threat groups named in QuoIntelligence's June 2021 report “E.K.P. & Agent Tesla: The Daily Operations of a Nigerian eCrime Gang” does MITRE ATT&CK record as using the largest number of the techniques the report describes?
questions.reference_answer: G0037 FIN6: ATT&CK records FIN6 as using 12 of the 35 techniques the report describes (T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information (through its sub-technique T1027.010 Command Obfuscation), T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation, T1048 Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol (through its sub-technique T1048.003 Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol), T1053 Scheduled Task/Job (through its sub-technique T1053.005 Scheduled Task), T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter, T1087 Account Discovery (through its sub-technique T1087.002 Domain Account), T1204 User Execution (through its sub-technique T1204.002 Malicious File), T1547 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution (through its sub-technique T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder), T1555 Credentials from Password Stores, T1560 Archive Collected Data, T1566 Phishing (through its sub-techniques T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment and T1566.003 Spearphishing via Service) and T1685 Disable or Modify Tools). G0080 Cobalt Group uses 11. G0120 Evilnum uses 6.
questions.cypher:
CYPHER 25
MATCH (g:`Group`)-[u:`USES`]->(:`Technique`)-[:`SUBTECHNIQUE_OF`*0..1]->(t:`Technique`)
WHERE g.`attack_id` IN $groups AND t.`attack_id` IN $techniques AND u.`source` = 'attack'
WITH g, collect(DISTINCT t.`attack_id`) AS used
WITH max(size(used)) AS most, collect({id: g.`attack_id`, used: used}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row, most WHERE size(row.used) = most
RETURN row.id AS answer, row.used AS support
ORDER BY answer

questions.question: Which of the techniques described in Intel 471's December 2021 report “How the new Emotet differs from previous versions” are missing from MITRE ATT&CK's record of the techniques Emotet uses?
questions.reference_answer: 3 of the 13 techniques the report describes are not among the techniques ATT&CK records for Emotet: T1001 Data Obfuscation, T1189 Drive-by Compromise and T1606 Forge Web Credentials. ATT&CK records Emotet as using the other 10: T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information (through its sub-techniques T1027.001 Binary Padding, T1027.002 Software Packing, T1027.009 Embedded Payloads, T1027.010 Command Obfuscation and T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File), T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, T1055 Process Injection (through its sub-techniques T1055.001 Dynamic-link Library Injection and T1055.012 Process Hollowing), T1057 Process Discovery, T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter (through its sub-techniques T1059.001 PowerShell, T1059.003 Windows Command Shell and T1059.005 Visual Basic), T1110 Brute Force (through its sub-technique T1110.001 Password Guessing), T1114 Email Collection, T1218 System Binary Proxy Execution (through its sub-technique T1218.010 Regsvr32), T1566 Phishing (through its sub-techniques T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment and T1566.002 Spearphishing Link) and T1573 Encrypted Channel.
questions.cypher:
CYPHER 25
MATCH (t:`Technique`)
WHERE t.`attack_id` IN $techniques
  AND NOT EXISTS {
    MATCH (:`Software` {`attack_id`: $user})-[u:`USES`]->(:`Technique`)-[:`SUBTECHNIQUE_OF`*0..1]->(t)
    WHERE u.`source` = 'attack'
  }
RETURN t.`attack_id` AS answer
ORDER BY answer

questions.question: Which threat groups does MITRE ATT&CK record as using every technique described in Proofpoint's January 2022 report “OiVaVoii – An Active Malicious Hybrid Cloud Threats Campaign”?
questions.reference_answer: Only one group in ATT&CK uses all 4 techniques the report describes: G0007 APT28 (T1078 Valid Accounts, T1528 Steal Application Access Token, T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle (through its sub-technique T1557.004 Evil Twin) and T1566 Phishing (through its sub-technique T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment)).
questions.cypher:
CYPHER 25
MATCH (g:`Group`)-[u:`USES`]->(:`Technique`)-[:`SUBTECHNIQUE_OF`*0..1]->(t:`Technique`)
WHERE t.`attack_id` IN $techniques AND u.`source` = 'attack'
WITH g, count(DISTINCT t) AS covered
WHERE covered = size($techniques)
RETURN g.`attack_id` AS answer
ORDER BY answer
